newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec's Lucien Bouchard warns of public debt trap.
newsitem.headline: Quebec's Lucien Bouchard warns of public debt trap.

text.p: Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard said on Tuesday that high public debt and unemployment were weighing heavily on the French-speaking province's development.
"All of Quebec society is trapped by Quebec's indebtedness, by the deficit and by unemployment," Bouchard said in a speech in the Montreal suburb of Laval.

In a keynote address on his government's economic policy, Bouchard repeated that the province would meet its 1996/97 budget deficit targets, despite certain "difficulties" on the government revenue side.

Quebec has forecast a budget deficit of C$3.2 billion for fiscal 1996/97, down from C$3.9 billion in 1995/96 ended March 31. Quebec's first-quarter revenues were 7.5 percent below year earlier levels.
Aside from blaming the Canadian government for aggravating Quebec's situation by reducing cash transfers to the province, Bouchard called on Quebec business leaders to help spur economic development.
"We also ask business leaders to take a little pain to better help spread the growth among a greater number of Quebec men and women," Bouchard said in French.
Bouchard said that the coming year would be the most difficult period in the cleanup of government finances, but added that the province must stay the course.
Of Quebec's C$40 billion in expenditures forecast for 1997/98, C$13 billion will be for health services, C$9 billion for education and slightly more than C$6 billion for debt service charges.
Quebec has about C$75 billion of direct debt at the provincial level and another C$25 billion at the municipal level, not including debt at the government-owned electrical utility Hydro-Quebec.

Bouchard said Quebec's "social-democratic" policies are suffering under the debt burden and unemployment levels and that with personal and corporate taxation at already high levels, the province has little rooom to manoeuver.

Bouchard ruled out taxing more heavily the province's wealthier residents and said Quebec would take measures to help business, such as reducing the government regulatory burden, financing export activities and favouring innovation, job creation and worker training. Those measures will be discussed at a government-sponsored socio-economic conference in Montreal at the end of October.
In his speech, Bouchard did not mention his government's drive for Quebec separation from Canada, but he said a stronger economic and fiscal environment would restore Quebec's "freedom."
"A greater freedom for Quebec society that would be able to make important political choices, knowing it is on solid ground," Bouchard said.
Bouchard has been Quebec premier since January 29. He is credited with leading separatists to near victory in the October 1995 referendum on Quebec sovereignty.
